# TDPdf v1.31.0.0

**A curated sync with upstream [KillerPDF](https://github.com/SteveTheKiller/KillerPDF) v1.8.3–v1.8.5.** Upstream has replaced its PDF engine and restructured its source tree since the last sync, so nothing here was copied across — every item was reimplemented against TDPdf's own architecture. Reviewing our code against theirs also turned up four defects of our own, including one that could cost you a document.

## The important one

### A failed save could truncate the file you already had

TDPdf wrote each save directly over your existing document. If anything went wrong part-way through — and there is a known class of malformed PDF that does exactly that — the file was left cut short. Worse, the automatic retry then ran over the already-damaged file.

The window was small, but the loss was total and silent, because the only copy of the document was the one being written over.

Saves now write to a temporary file alongside the destination and move it into place only once it is complete. A failure now leaves your original untouched. Where the filesystem supports it, the move also preserves the file's permissions and its Mark of the Web rather than replacing them.

## Fixed

### Inserting a blank page threw away every unsaved annotation

Inserting a page renumbers the pages after it, but does not change how any of them look — so the annotations on those pages were still perfectly valid. They were being discarded anyway, because a page had been added somewhere else in the document.

They are now renumbered and kept. The undo history is renumbered with them, which fixes a quieter version of the same bug: an undo after an insert could restore one page's annotations onto its neighbour.

### Save Flattened distorted rotated and cropped pages

The rebuilt pages were sized from the raw page box. That ignores a quarter-turn a page inherits from its parent, and ignores the crop box entirely — so a landscape page could come back stretched onto a portrait sheet. Flatten now uses the same rotation- and crop-aware geometry the viewer, the link overlays and redaction already share.

### File names with underscores lost them

`My_Report.pdf` appeared as `MyReport.pdf` with the R underlined, in the recent-files list and the tab overflow menu — a menu reads an underscore as a keyboard-accelerator marker.

### Installing with a protected document open relaunched onto a file that was gone

After opening a password-protected PDF, TDPdf works against a decrypted copy in `%TEMP%`. Installing from that state told the newly installed copy to open the temporary file, which the closing process had just deleted.

### The keyboard shortcut list was missing two tools

Redact and Form fields were absent from the printed shortcut list. Both tools work and both were already correct in the on-screen keyboard view; only the list was stale.

## Added

### Each tab keeps its own place and zoom

Switching between open documents used to carry one document's zoom onto the next and drop you wherever the re-render landed. Each tab now resumes where you left it.

What has *not* changed is where a newly opened document starts: that is still the zoom or fit you last chose deliberately, applied across the app, so you do not re-pick Fit Page for every manual you open. A remembered fit is still replayed as a fit rather than as the number it produced — which is what stops a document opening enormous or microscopic when the window or the monitor has changed.

### Smaller files from scanned documents

A page that was already a JPEG scan now stays a JPEG through Save Flattened instead of being re-encoded as 24-bit colour, and a flattened page that is purely black and white is stored as a 1-bit image — roughly a twentyfold reduction on scanned text.

Both tests are deliberately conservative. A page only counts as a scan if essentially all of it is one JPEG, because re-encoding text or line art as JPEG damages it permanently. A single nearly-black pixel is enough for a page to take the lossless path. A larger file is a far better outcome than a degraded one.

### Smaller things

- **Open Containing Folder** on the document tab menu. It reveals the file you opened, not the working copy TDPdf keeps in `%TEMP%` for protected or edited documents.
- **Ctrl+R** and **Ctrl+Shift+R** rotate the selected pages clockwise and counter-clockwise.
- **Insert Blank Page takes a custom size**, in inches, millimetres or points, alongside the existing presets.
- **A page-size readout in the footer**, cycling pixels, inches, millimetres and points as you click it, remembered between sessions.
- **The image-export and Transform dialogs say how many pixels you will get** for the DPI you picked, instead of only the DPI.

## Not included

Several things upstream shipped in this range are deliberately absent: anything requiring tagged-PDF structure support, cryptographic signature revisions (TDPdf's signatures are drawn or imported images, not certificates), clipboard image pasting, a replacement file picker, a portable data folder, startup update checks — Intune and the Microsoft Store already handle that for TDPdf — and all localization and third-party packaging. The full list, with the reasoning for each, is in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Installing

Managed machines update through Intune automatically; nothing to do. Otherwise it is the same self-contained `TDPdf.exe`.
